### Start the Meteor build process

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/guides/meteor

Run the local development build server using npm run start.

```bash
npm run start
```

--------------------------------

### Install Tailwind CSS and initialize configuration

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/guides/adonisjs

Install tailwindcss, postcss, and autoprefixer as dev dependencies, then generate tailwind.config.js and postcss.config.js.

```shell
npm install -D tailwindcss@3 postcss autoprefixernpx tailwindcss init -p
```

--------------------------------

### Set starting color with from-*

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/gradient-color-stops

Use the from-* utility to define the starting color of a gradient.

```html
<div class="bg-gradient-to-r from-indigo-500 ..."></div>
```

--------------------------------

### Install Tailwind CSS and initialize configuration

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/guides/remix

Install tailwindcss, postcss, and autoprefixer as dev dependencies, then generate tailwind.config.ts and postcss.config.js.

```shell
npm install -D tailwindcss@3 postcss autoprefixernpx tailwindcss init --ts -p
```

--------------------------------

### Start development server

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/guides/solidjs

Run the development build process to view the project with Tailwind styles active.

```shell
npm run dev

```

--------------------------------

### Start the development build process

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/guides/adonisjs

Run the project's build process to compile CSS and watch for changes during development.

```shell
npm run dev
```

--------------------------------

### Pack rows to the start using content-start

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/align-content

Use `content-start` to pack rows in a container against the start of the cross axis.

```html
<div class="h-56 grid grid-cols-3 gap-4 content-start ...">
  <div>01</div>
  <div>02</div>
  <div>03</div>
  <div>04</div>
  <div>05</div>
</div>
```

--------------------------------

### Start Phoenix development server

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/guides/phoenix

Runs the Phoenix development server using mix phx.server to compile assets and start watching for changes.

```shell
mix phx.server
```

--------------------------------

### Align content to start with place-content-start

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/place-content

Packs items against the start of the block axis.

```html
<div class="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4 place-content-start h-48 ...">
  <div>01</div>
  <div>02</div>
  <div>03</div>
  <div>04</div>
</div>
```

### Start the Tailwind CLI build process with --watch

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/installation

Runs the CLI to scan template files and build compiled CSS to the designated output file while watching for changes.

```bash
npx tailwindcss -i ./src/input.css -o ./src/output.css --watch
```

--------------------------------

### Start build process with npm run watch

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/guides/symfony

Runs the Webpack build watcher to automatically recompile assets on file changes.

```terminal
npm run watch
```

--------------------------------

### Install and configure postcss-nesting with tailwindcss/nesting

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/using-with-preprocessors

Install postcss-nesting to use standard CSS Nesting syntax and pass it as an argument to tailwindcss/nesting in your PostCSS configuration.

```bash
npm install -D postcss-nesting
```

```javascript
// postcss.config.js
module.exports = {
  plugins: {
    'postcss-import': {},
    'tailwindcss/nesting': 'postcss-nesting',
    tailwindcss: {},
    autoprefixer: {},
  }
}
```

--------------------------------

### Install and configure @tailwindcss/typography plugin

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/typography-plugin

Install the typography plugin package via npm and register it in your main style.css file using the @plugin directive.

```shell
npm install -D @tailwindcss/typography
```

```css
  @import "tailwindcss";
+ @plugin "@tailwindcss/typography";
```

--------------------------------

### Install and configure Autoprefixer for PostCSS

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/browser-support

Install Autoprefixer as a development dependency and add it to the end of the plugin list in your PostCSS configuration to automatically handle vendor prefixes.

```shell
npm install -D autoprefixer
```

```javascript
module.exports = {
  plugins: {
    tailwindcss: {},
    autoprefixer: {},
  }
}
```

```vue
<template>
  <h1 class="text-3xl font-bold underline">
    Hello world!
  </h1>
</template>

```

### Vendor prefix example for background-clip

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/browser-support

Demonstrates vendor prefixes required by modern browsers for specific CSS properties like background-clip.

```css
.bg-clip-text {
  -webkit-background-clip: text;
  background-clip: text;
}
```

--------------------------------

### Setting starting and ending lines with col-start-* and col-end-*

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/grid-column

Use col-start-* and col-end-* utilities to make an element start or end at a specific grid line. CSS grid lines start at 1, so a full-width item in a 6-column grid starts at line 1 and ends at line 7.

```html
<div class="grid grid-cols-6 gap-4">
  <div class="col-start-2 col-span-4 ...">01</div>
  <div class="col-start-1 col-end-3 ...">02</div>
  <div class="col-end-7 col-span-2 ...">03</div>
  <div class="col-start-1 col-end-7 ...">04</div>
</div>
```

### Align item to the start using self-start

```html
  <div>03</div>
</div>
```

```javascript
}
```

### Set percentage widths with w-fraction utilities

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/width

Use utilities like w-full, w-1/2, and w-2/5 to set an element to a percentage-based width.

```html
<div class="flex ...">
  <div class="w-1/2 ... ">w-1/2</div>
  <div class="w-1/2 ... ">w-1/2</div>
</div>
<div class="flex ...">
  <div class="w-2/5 ...">w-2/5</div>
  <div class="w-3/5 ...">w-3/5</div>
</div>
<div class="flex ...">
  <div class="w-1/3 ...">w-1/3</div>
  <div class="w-2/3 ...">w-2/3</div>
</div>
<div class="flex ...">
  <div class="w-1/4 ...">w-1/4</div>
  <div class="w-3/4 ...">w-3/4</div>
</div>
<div class="flex ...">
  <div class="w-1/5 ...">w-1/5</div>
  <div class="w-4/5 ...">w-4/5</div>
</div>
<div class="flex ...">
  <div class="w-1/6 ...">w-1/6</div>
  <div class="w-5/6 ...">w-5/6</div>
</div>
<div class="w-full ...">w-full</div>
```

--------------------------------

### Register official plugins in tailwind.config.js

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/plugins

Add official plugins to your Tailwind CSS configuration after installing them via npm.

```javascript
/** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */
module.exports = {
  // ...
  plugins: [
    require('@tailwindcss/typography'),
    require('@tailwindcss/forms'),
    require('@tailwindcss/aspect-ratio'),
    require('@tailwindcss/container-queries'),
  ]
}
```

### Apply background size responsively

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/background-size

Use breakpoint prefixes such as `md:` to apply background size utilities at specific screen widths and above.

```html
<div class="bg-auto md:bg-contain">
  <!-- ... -->
</div>

```

--------------------------------

### Set fixed widths with w-* utilities

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/width

Use utilities like w-px, w-1, and w-64 to set an element to a fixed width.

```html
<div class="w-96 ...">w-96</div>
<div class="w-80 ...">w-80</div>
<div class="w-64 ...">w-64</div>
<div class="w-48 ...">w-48</div>
<div class="w-40 ...">w-40</div>
<div class="w-32 ...">w-32</div>
<div class="w-24 ...">w-24</div>
```

--------------------------------

### Apply text-balance conditionally at responsive breakpoints

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/text-wrap

Uses responsive variant modifiers like md: to apply text-balance starting at medium screen sizes and above.

```html
<h1 class="text-wrap md:text-balance">
  <!-- ... -->
</h1>
```

--------------------------------

### Using arbitrary transition delay values

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/transition-delay

Use square bracket notation to generate a transition-delay utility on the fly with any arbitrary value.

```html
<div class="delay-[2000ms]">
  <!-- ... -->
</div>

```

--------------------------------

### Set border width using logical properties

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/border-width

Use border-s-* and border-e-* to set inline start and end border widths, which adapt to text direction.

```html
<div dir="ltr">
  <div class="border-s-4 ..."></div>
<div>

<div dir="rtl">
  <div class="border-s-4 ..."></div>
<div>
```

### Build a responsive marketing card layout

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/responsive-design

Uses `md:flex` and responsive size utilities to shift from a stacked layout on small screens to a side-by-side layout on medium screens and larger.

```html
<div class="max-w-md mx-auto bg-white rounded-xl shadow-md overflow-hidden md:max-w-2xl">
  <div class="md:flex">
    <div class="md:shrink-0">
      <img class="h-48 w-full object-cover md:h-full md:w-48" src="/img/building.jpg" alt="Modern building architecture">
    </div>
    <div class="p-8">
      <div class="uppercase tracking-wide text-sm text-indigo-500 font-semibold">Company retreats</div>
      <a href="#" class="block mt-1 text-lg leading-tight font-medium text-black hover:underline">Incredible accommodation for your team</a>
      <p class="mt-2 text-slate-500">Looking to take your team away on a retreat to enjoy awesome food and take in some sunshine? We have a list of places to do just that.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

--------------------------------

### Add Tailwind plugin to mix.exs dependencies

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/guides/phoenix

Adds the :tailwind package to deps in mix.exs for dev environment execution. Run mix deps.get afterward to install.

```elixir
defp deps do
  [
    {:tailwind, "~> 0.1", runtime: Mix.env() == :dev}
  ]
end

```

--------------------------------

### CSS-only abstraction example with duplicated HTML

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/reusing-styles

Illustrates why CSS-only class abstractions require duplicating HTML structure across templates whenever the component is used.

```html
<!-- Even with custom CSS, you still need to duplicate this HTML structure -->
<div class="chat-notification">
  <div class="chat-notification-logo-wrapper">
    <img class="chat-notification-logo" src="/img/logo.svg" alt="ChitChat Logo">
  </div>
  <div class="chat-notification-content">
    <div class="chat-notification-title">ChitChat</div>
    <p class="chat-notification-message">You have a new message!</p>
  </div>
</div>

<style>
  .chat-notification { /* ... */ }
  .chat-notification-logo-wrapper { /* ... */ }
  .chat-notification-logo { /* ... */ }
  .chat-notification-content { /* ... */ }
  .chat-notification-title { /* ... */ }
  .chat-notification-message { /* ... */ }
</style>
```

--------------------------------

### Include public HTML entry point in content configuration

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/content-configuration

Include HTML files located in framework entry directories such as public/index.html if they contain Tailwind class names.

```javascript
module.exports = {
  content: [
    './public/index.html',
    './src/**/*.{html,js}',
  ],
  // ...
}
```

--------------------------------

### Creating a responsive profile card with utility classes

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/utility-first

Constructs a responsive profile card component using utility classes for layout, spacing, typography, and interactive button states. Utilizes responsive modifiers (sm:) and pseudo-class variants (hover:, focus:) to handle state styling without inline styles.

```html
<div class="py-8 px-8 max-w-sm mx-auto space-y-2 bg-white rounded-xl shadow-lg sm:py-4 sm:flex sm:items-center sm:space-y-0 sm:gap-x-6">
  <img class="block mx-auto h-24 rounded-full sm:mx-0 sm:shrink-0" src="/img/erin-lindford.jpg" alt="Woman's Face" />
  <div class="text-center space-y-2 sm:text-left">
    <div class="space-y-0.5">
      <p class="text-lg text-black font-semibold">
        Erin Lindford
      </p>
      <p class="text-slate-500 font-medium">
        Product Engineer
      </p>
    </div>
    <button class="px-4 py-1 text-sm text-purple-600 font-semibold rounded-full border border-purple-200 hover:text-white hover:bg-purple-600 hover:border-transparent focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-purple-600 focus:ring-offset-2">Message</button>
  </div>
</div>
```

```html
<div class="pointer-events-none md:pointer-events-auto">
  <!-- ... -->

```

--------------------------------

### Positioning with row-start-* and row-end-*

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/grid-row

Use row-start-* and row-end-* utilities to position an element at specific grid lines. Note that CSS grid lines start at 1, not 0.

```html
<div class="grid grid-rows-3 grid-flow-col gap-4">
  <div class="row-start-2 row-span-2 ...">01</div>
  <div class="row-end-3 row-span-2 ...">02</div>
  <div class="row-start-1 row-end-4 ...">03</div>
</div>
```

--------------------------------

### Configuring postcss-import for multi-file CSS setups

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/adding-custom-styles

Use `postcss-import` to combine multiple CSS files into a single stylesheet before Tailwind processes them to avoid `@layer` directive errors.

```javascript
module.exports = {
  plugins: {
    'postcss-import': {},
    tailwindcss: {},
    autoprefixer: {},
  }
}

```

--------------------------------

### Create and consume a custom preset

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/presets

Define a preset configuration object with custom theme settings and plugins in `my-preset.js`, then require it under the `presets` array in `tailwind.config.js` to extend it with project-specific rules.

```javascript
// Example preset
module.exports = {
  theme: {
    colors: {
      blue: {
        light: '#85d7ff',
        DEFAULT: '#1fb6ff',
        dark: '#009eeb',
      },
      pink: {
        light: '#ff7ce5',
        DEFAULT: '#ff49db',
        dark: '#ff16d1',
      },
      gray: {
        darkest: '#1f2d3d',
        dark: '#3c4858',
        DEFAULT: '#c0ccda',
        light: '#e0e6ed',
        lightest: '#f9fafc',
      }
    },
    fontFamily: {
      sans: ['Graphik', 'sans-serif'],
    },
    extend: {
      flexGrow: {
        2: '2',
        3: '3',
      },
      zIndex: {
        60: '60',
        70: '70',
        80: '80',
        90: '90',
        100: '100',
      },
    }
  },
  plugins: [
    require('@tailwindcss/typography'),
    require('@tailwindcss/aspect-ratio'),
  ],
}
```

```javascript
/** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */
module.exports = {
  presets: [
    require('./my-preset.js')
  ],
  // Customizations specific to this project would go here
  theme: {
    extend: {
      minHeight: {
        48: '12rem',
      }
    }
  },
}
```

```html
<div class="drop-shadow-md md:drop-shadow-xl">
```

--------------------------------

### Merge corePlugins across preset and config using an object

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/presets

Configure corePlugins as an object in both your preset and tailwind.config.js to merge the settings together. In this setup, both the float and cursor core plugins will be disabled.

```javascript
module.exports = {
  // ...
  corePlugins: {
    float: false,
  },
}
```

```javascript
/** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */
module.exports = {
  presets: [
    require('./my-preset.js'),
  ],
  // This configuration will be merged
  corePlugins: {
    cursor: false
  }
}
```

--------------------------------

### Example text triggering unintended class generation in HTML

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/content-configuration

Illustrates how plain text containing words that match utility names (such as 'container') can cause Tailwind to unintentionally generate CSS classes.

```html
<div class="text-lg leading-8 text-gray-600">
  Every custom pool we design starts as a used shipping container, and is
  retrofitted with state of the art technology and finishes to turn it into
  a beautiful and functional way to entertain your guests all summer long.
</div>
```

--------------------------------

### Applying arbitrary backdrop brightness values

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/backdrop-brightness

Use square bracket notation to generate backdrop-brightness utilities on the fly using arbitrary values.



--------------------------------

### Register dynamic utilities with matchUtilities

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/plugins

Registers dynamic utility classes that map to theme configuration values using `matchUtilities`. Automatically supports arbitrary value syntax.

```javascript
const plugin = require('tailwindcss/plugin')

module.exports = {
  theme: {
    tabSize: {
      1: '1',
      2: '2',
      4: '4',
      8: '8',
    }
  },
  plugins: [
    plugin(function({ matchUtilities, theme }) {
      matchUtilities(
        { preserve:
          tab: (value) => ({
            tabSize: value
          }),
        },
        { values: theme('tabSize') }
      )
    })
  ]
}
```

--------------------------------

### Define a configurable plugin with plugin.withOptions

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/plugins

Use plugin.withOptions to define plugins that accept user options for customizing generated classes and theme settings.

```javascript
const plugin = require('tailwindcss/plugin')

module.exports = plugin.withOptions(function (options = {}) {
  return function({ addComponents }) {
    const className = options.className ?? 'markdown'

    addComponents({
      [`.${className}`]: {
        // ...
      }
    })
  }
}, function (options) {
  return {
    theme: {
      markdown: {
        // ...
      }
    },
  }
})
```

### Demonstrate CSS rule declaration order and specificity

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/adding-custom-styles

Illustrates how stylesheet order dictates which declaration wins when selectors share identical specificity.

```css

  background: blue;
  /* ... */
}

.bg-black {
  background: black;
}
```

```html

<button class="ease-out duration-300 ...">Button B</button>
<button class="ease-in-out duration-300 ...">Button C</button>
```

### Configure template paths in tailwind.config.js

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/guides/qwik

Specifies the paths to all Qwik template and source files in the Tailwind configuration.

```javascript
/** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */
module.exports = {
  content: ['./src/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx,mdx}'],
  theme: {
    extend: {},
  },
  plugins: [],
}

```

### Target mobile screens with unprefixed utilities

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/responsive-design

Use unprefixed utility classes to style for mobile screens by default, then override them at larger breakpoints like sm:.

```html

<div class="text-center sm:text-left"></div>
```

### Enable PostCSS in svelte.config.js

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/guides/sveltekit

Imports `vitePreprocess` in `svelte.config.js` to allow processing `<style>` blocks as PostCSS.

```javascript
import adapter from '@sveltejs/adapter-auto';
import { vitePreprocess } from '@sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte';
/** @type {import('@sveltejs/kit').Config} */
const config = {
  kit: {
    adapter: adapter()
  },
  preprocess: vitePreprocess()
};
export default config;

```

### Customize gridRowStart in tailwind.config.js

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/grid-row

Extends the gridRowStart configuration in tailwind.config.js to add custom row-start-* utilities.

```javascript
module.exports = {
  theme: {
    extend: {
      gridRowStart: {
        '8': '8',
        '9': '9',
        '10': '10',
        '11': '11',
        '12': '12',
        '13': '13',
      }
    }
  }
}

```

### Configure source paths for pages and components

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/content-configuration

Configure glob patterns in the content array to match HTML and JavaScript template files.

```javascript
/** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */
module.exports = {
  content: [
    './pages/**/*.{html,js}',
    './components/**/*.{html,js}'
  ],
  // ...
}
```

--------------------------------

### List root HTML files specifically in content configuration

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/content-configuration

Explicitly list root files like index.html alongside specific directory glob patterns instead of using an overly broad pattern.

```javascript
/** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */
module.exports = {
  content: [
    './components/**/*.{html,js}',
    './pages/**/*.{html,js}',
    './index.html',
  ],
  // ...
}
```

### Set flex item to flex-initial

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/flex

Use flex-initial to allow a flex item to shrink but not grow, sizing according to its initial dimensions.

```html
<div class="flex">
  <div class="flex-none w-14 ...">
    01
  </div>
  <div class="flex-initial w-64 ...">
    02
  </div>
  <div class="flex-initial w-32 ...">
    03
  </div>
</div>
```

--------------------------------

### Apply logical floats with float-start

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/float

Use logical property utilities like float-start and float-end to float elements based on the document or element text direction (LTR vs RTL).

```html
<img class="float-start ..." src="path/to/image.jpg">
<p>Maybe we can live without libraries, people like you and me. ...</p>

<img class="float-start ..." src="path/to/image.jpg">
<p dir="rtl">... ربما يمكننا العيش بدون مكتبات، أشخاص مثلي ومثلك. ربما. بالتأكيد </p>
```

```css
}
```

### Resolving overlapping configurations across presets

Source: https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/presets

Demonstrates preset ordering where overlapping configurations are resolved with the last configuration taking precedence.

```javascript
/** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */
module.exports = {
  presets: [
    require('@acmecorp/configuration-a'),
    require('@acmecorp/configuration-b'),
  ]
}
```
